subject: Post-call summary: cost constraints, levers, and next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Becker <tom.becker@gateone.com>, Sara Lim <sara.lim@gateone.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call summary: cost constraints, levers, and next steps

Tom / Sara — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Token spend unpredictability: bursts from nightly reconciliation jobs are blowing monthly budgets.
- High per-token cost on embeddings/LLM routes used for fraud scoring and email summarization.
- Latency spikes exceeding product SLOs (p50 target < 200ms; you've seen p50 ~ 350ms during peak).
- Procurement window: limited budget for Q3; any pilot needs to show clear < 60% cost delta vs current run-rate or be justifyable via ops savings.

Goals we heard:
- Reduce unit inference cost for your summarization pipeline by ~50–60% while keeping quality and latency within the current thresholds.
- Put a 6–8 week pilot in place with production-like traffic for the billing routes so you can validate cost + quality.
- Get minimal legal/PO paperwork completed in July to enable a pilot start first week of August.

Primary levers we recommended (high level):
1) Dedicated reserved capacity for high-volume inference routes — predictable throughput and credits on committed spend.
2) Batching and continuous KV caching for prefix-heavy summaries — expected token reduction 20–35% on average.
3) Quantized model variant for reranking/low-context calls to shave per-token execution cost ~25–40% (with a small eval to confirm quality).
4) Workload routing: route lower-priority reconciliation requests to lower-cost model tier during off-peak.

Preliminary TCO sketch (attached spreadsheet has full lines):
- Baseline: ~18M tokens/day across summarization + embeddings, current cost ~$22k/day (public vendor rate).
- Conservative Redwood estimate (reserved + batching + quantization mix): ~$8.5k/day (~61% reduction).
- Upside: with aggressive caching and model tuning could drop to ~$6.9k/day.

Immediate next steps (action owners & dates):
- Redwood to share the attached TCO workbook + recommended pilot config (Vanessa) — by EOD Tue 2028-07-02. (attachment: gateone_postcall_tco_v1.xlsx)
- GateOne to share sample traffic profile for the summarization route + a sample of prompt sets for quality checks (Tom / Sara) — by Fri 2028-07-05.
- Legal / Procurement request: GateOne to send a contact for PO and required terms; Redwood will surface a short pilot SOW and order form (Marissa) — target 2028-07-12.
- Technical: schedule a 45-min pilot design call next week to lock the endpoints, SLAs, and success metrics (Ben to propose times).

Attachments: gateone_postcall_tco_v1.xlsx, redwood_batching_levers.pdf

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this into a short pilot so you can validate the unit economics.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0143

From: Tom Becker <tom.becker@gateone.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@gateone.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call summary: cost constraints, levers, and next steps

Vanessa — this lines up with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications before we go deep: 
1) The 18M tokens/day number — is that including embeddings for the fraud model? Our embeddings spike separately and account for ~30% of the cost.
2) For reserved capacity: what's the minimum monthly commitment you'd expect for the reductions you listed? Our procurement team will need a hard floor for negotiations.

I'll pull together the traffic dump and prompt samples. Procurement: please loop in Alicia (cc'd on a follow-up) — she owns contract reviews.

Tom
Tom Becker
CTO, GateOne Inc.
Tom.Becker@gateone.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Becker <tom.becker@gateone.com>, Sara Lim <sara.lim@gateone.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call summary: cost constraints, levers, and next steps

Tom — answers inline + added a small clarifying table in the attached workbook.

1) Embeddings: the 18M/day figure includes embeddings. In the workbook we split the two buckets: summarization (LLM generate) ~12.6M tokens/day; embeddings ~5.4M tokens/day. Embeddings cost profile is different (higher per-token) and we model them on a separate pipeline with quantized vector models + caching to cut 40–55% on that bucket.

2) Minimum commitment: for the conservative ~61% reduction we modeled a 3-month reserved commitment at ~40% of your current monthly spend (we can structure as a ramp). Rough floor in the workbook: $150k/month committed to get the stated discounts; there are options to scale the commitment down if you accept a longer evaluation period with usage-based true-ups — we outline 3 commitment tiers in the sheet.

Quick notes on quality risk and tests:
- We will run an A/B eval during the pilot: baseline model vs quantized variant on a held-out sample of 1k user interactions to measure quality delta; if the delta is >2% on the metrics you care about we won't route production traffic to the quantized model.
- For latency SLOs: dedicated pools + continuous batching keep p50 below 200ms in our benchmarks for workloads with similar sequence lengths; we'll run a short soak test on your traffic profile.

I've attached the workbook (gateone_postcall_tco_v1.xlsx) and a short one-pager on batching/caching levers (redwood_batching_levers.pdf).

Proposed times for the pilot design call: Wed 2028-07-03 09:00–09:45 PT or Thu 2028-07-04 11:00–11:45 PT. Ben will send a calendar invite.

—
Vanessa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Becker <tom.becker@gateone.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call summary: cost constraints, levers, and next steps

Tom — looping in a very short checklist so procurement has what they need for an internal PO review: 
- Pilot SOW (one-page) + order form (we'll draft and share by 2028-07-05).
- Pilot acceptance criteria: 6-week run, cost delta target (>=50% reduction vs baseline), latency p50 < 200ms, quality within 2% of baseline on your NPS-style metric.
- Billing model for pilot: blended reserved + usage true-up; pilot credits available to offset setup.

If the checklist looks good I’ll draft the SOW and Marissa will include standard pilot terms. Thanks — I'll push a calendar invite for the Wed 09:00 PT slot now.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
